text: One more thing from that same pass, and it is a distinction that will save you a lot of wasted afternoons.
While it was testing the keyboard it noticed that two of the arrow keys do the same thing. Right and down move the card the same way, which looks wrong. A reasonable person would file that as a bug.

It did not. It went and checked how the library it is using is meant to behave, found that the library walks through the cards in a single line rather than treating the board as a grid, and concluded that this is the documented design, not a fault.

So it wrote the finding down and moved on. Not everything that surprises you is broken. Some of it is a decision somebody else made on purpose, and the difference between those two is worth five minutes of checking before you ask for a fix.

This is the other half of the discipline. The four steps stop a tool claiming a fix it has not proved. This stops you demanding a fix for something that was never broken. Both failures cost the same afternoon.
